- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward buffer for 10–15 day horizon.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., >0.67 → <0.33), model lags in adjusting downward; apply early correction (day 2–3) to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overfit recent trends; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth out volatility.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in 5–10 day horizon.
